name: temp-por-top-release
description: Full four-cell assembly liveness check on design/netlist/temp_por_top.spice: cold start from 0 V with bias_core, temp_core, por_comparator and por_output_chain in the real top-level wiring, asking whether the shared IBIAS node survives the reset-asserted state and whether RESETn therefore releases and enables the sensor. This is the witness that the bias-vs-POR lockup DR-010 fixed is absent from the assembled block, not just from the two-cell integration testbench that found it. POST-LAYOUT: run against the extracted layout/postlayout/temp_por_top.spice, not the schematic export -- same stimulus, same manifest, same 81-point grid.
claim: spec/decision-records/DR-010-shared-ibias-disabled-consumer-contract.md -- the disabled-consumer high-impedance contract on the shared IBIAS net, measured on the full assembly. Also substantiates DR-005 startup ordering steps 4-6 end to end (bias core up, POR decides, sensor enabled only afterwards) and records the assembled block against spec/target-spec.md#por-iq in the state that row is defined in. Liveness and ordering only: the threshold itself is sim/por-comparator-designer-check/'s, the >=1 ms pulse width is sim/por-output-chain-pulse/'s, and the ramp-rate / brownout envelope is #14's. Deterministic corners only (design.ngspice sets sw_stat_mismatch=0), so it makes no distribution claim -- mismatch is #15's Monte Carlo job. Post-layout re-run (#87, under #18) against layout/postlayout/temp_por_top.spice (#82/PR #180 -- direct klt extraction, 'klt extract --parasitics' plus klt lvs's net correspondence, 159/159 nets paired): the same four-cell assembly with the real drawn interconnect R/C in the loop, including the cross-domain routing over the temp-sensing/always-on domain seam (IBIAS, RESETn/EN, VDD, VSS) that a schematic netlist cannot see at all. Supersedes the schematic-level record 20260802-205904-bdc077d; the schematic-vs-extracted delta is written up in design/temp_por_top.md.
netlist_provenance_note: temp_por_top: 239 drawn devices, 0 ideal -- every golden device, including instance xtemp's XCC (cap_mim_2f0_m3m4_noshield, on xtemp__PG/xtemp__NZ), is now drawn and routed to its schematic nets (DR-028, #259); temp_core's layout previously reserved floor area for it (#177) but no longer does, so any claim that rests on the amplifier's compensation pole is a genuine post-layout claim, not a schematic one. 136/145 nets carry parasitic R/C across 272 cards (SigmaR 280929 Ohm, SigmaC 5900.6 fF); the 9 nets without are isolated well/plate nets and the substrate global. 9 body/well/plate ties (vsubs -> VSS, the four sub-cells' NW*/NWQ nets) are tied where the schematic puts them rather than where the extraction found them, because the extraction deck's connectivity stack does not reach them -- MiM plates no longer need this treatment (klayout-tools#314, closed and fixed; #264/#259 routed every drawn plate in this block onto its own schematic node). 27 resistors extracted as ppolyf_u_1k are emitted as ppolyf_u_3k (klayout-tools#323) and 8 MiM caps extracted as cap_mim_2f0_m4m5_noshield are emitted as cap_mim_2f0_m3m4_noshield (klayout-tools#315) -- the drawn geometry is the schematic's in both cases, only the deck's name for it differs. Per layout/postlayout/AUDIT.md.
analyses: meas tran iq_pre avg i(vsup) from=1.5m to=1.9m
meas tran vrst_pre find v(resetn) at=1.9m
meas tran vib_pre find v(xdut.ibias) at=1.9m
meas tran vref_pre find v(xdut.vref) at=1.9m
meas tran vptat_pre find v(ptat) at=1.9m
meas tran trel when v(resetn)=1.0 rise=1
meas tran vrst_post find v(resetn) at=28m
meas tran vib_post find v(xdut.ibias) at=28m
meas tran vptat_post find v(ptat) at=28m
meas tran vctat_post find v(ctat) at=28m

vibias_asserted_v.description: THE DR-010 CHECK, on the full assembly. The shared IBIAS node with the real disabled temp_core hanging on it, in the reset-asserted state. It used to sit at 1.0-6.6 mV at every one of the 81 points (sim/bias-core-ibias-sharing/records/20260801-054722-6cf5898.md) because temp_core's ENB-gated XMDIB shorted it to VSS; bounding it at a diode drop says the shared node must be ALIVE in exactly the state POR has to work in.

resetn_asserted_mv.description: no early release: RESETn is still a valid logic low with the rail settled and the one-shot still running (DR-004 active-low). Guards against the opposite failure to the lockup -- a block that releases reset before the bias core is up.

t_release_ms.description: THE LIVENESS CHECK. RESETn must actually release, at every corner, within the run. Before DR-010 this measurement did not exist at all: RESETn was never released at any point of the grid, so the loop never got here. Bounded loosely on purpose -- the accurate >=1 ms pulse-width claim is sim/por-output-chain-pulse/'s, measured from a stepped t0; this row only asks whether the block starts. The 29 ms ceiling is the run span minus the settled sample, so a corner that never releases fails rather than silently reporting the last time point.

resetn_released_v.description: spec/target-spec.md#por-drive: the deasserted state is actively driven to the rail into the 5 pF load, push-pull, not open-drain (DR-004).

vptat_asserted_mv.description: DR-005 startup ordering step 6, first half: while RESETn is asserted the sensor is genuinely off and its pad is held at VSS, not floating.

vptat_released_v.description: DR-005 startup ordering step 6, second half, and the end-to-end proof the lockup is gone: releasing RESETn really does enable temp_core and the PTAT output comes alive. That arrow is the one the old lockup closed on itself. The spread floor is a harness-integrity check -- a PTAT output that does not move with temperature means .temp or a .lib section failed to apply.

vctat_released_v.description: same, on the CTAT pad (VEB of temp_core's 1x PNP).

vref_asserted_v.description: bias_core's reference in the reset-asserted state. It was never the thing at fault -- the reference loop is self-biased and does not depend on the IBIAS leg's compliance -- and carrying it here keeps that separation visible on the assembled block too.

iq_por_ua.description: spec/target-spec.md#por-iq (<1 uA), the assembled block, in the state the row is defined in (section 5 rule 1: RESETn asserted, rail settled, sensor disabled). EXPECTED TO FAIL. This is the ALREADY-OWNED overrun design/bias_core.md 'Iq apportionment' records at 2.37x from the per-cell numbers; this row is the first time it is measured on the real assembly instead of summed across records. DR-010 does not address it and does not pretend to -- it is a magnitude problem pending its own re-cost decision record through #1, whereas DR-010 fixed a liveness defect. The check is left at the RATIFIED 1.0 uA and allowed to fail: per CLAUDE.md and target-spec.md section 5, the target is not relaxed to make a result pass.
